claim: An IB student applying to an Ontario university from outside Ontario is a Group B applicant, not Group A, and the two groups have different deadlines and different fees.
excerpt: You are a Group A applicant if all of the following are true: You are currently taking 1 or more Ontario high school courses and You are under 21 on or before December 31, 2026, and You have an OSSD or are working toward an OSSD with six 4U/M courses. You are a Group B applicant if you do not meet the Group A criteria. For example, you are: Not currently taking a course at an Ontario high school. A Canadian outside of Ontario. An international applicant. A postsecondary transfer student.
interpretation: This is the first thing to get right about Ontario and the thing most easily read past. Nearly every date published about applying to an Ontario university is a Group A date, written for a student sitting in an Ontario classroom. A Danish IB student is Group B. Group A's 15 January deadline is therefore not their deadline, and the absence of a Group B deadline is not permission to apply late — it means the university sets the date instead.

excerpt: January 15, 2027 The deadline for Group A applicants to submit their completed applications to the OUAC. [...] May 28, 2027 The latest date all Group A applicants who submitted their application by the January application deadline can expect a response from an Ontario university. [...] June 1, 2027 The earliest date a Group A applicant may be required to respond to an Ontario university offer of admission and give a financial commitment [...] Group B Applicants Application Deadlines There is no specific Undergraduate application deadline if you are a Group B applicant. Deadlines vary at each university and sometimes depend on the program. [...] You must ensure the OUAC has enough time to process your choices before the universities' program deadlines.
interpretation: Two separate things are being said and only one of them is a date. The Group A dates are real, published and not ours; they are recorded because they tell a Group B applicant when Ontario universities are actually deciding, which is the only reason to know them. The Group B statement is the finding: the OUAC declines to set a deadline, so the operative date is always the university's, and the OUAC adds a warning that it needs processing time of its own on top of that. That is why the route carries a no-central-deadline state and the real dates sit on the institutions.

interpretation: The advertised CAD 159 is not what a Group B applicant pays. Apply to four Ontario universities and the arithmetic is 159 plus 51 for the fourth choice plus four document evaluation fees, which is well over CAD 500 before a single university has read anything. The document evaluation fee is charged per university rather than per choice, so a second programme at the same university is comparatively cheap and a second university is not. That is a real planning fact and it is four clicks deep on the fees page.

claim: EducationPlannerBC is one account covering British Columbia's 25 public post-secondary institutions, with no limit on how many applications you submit through it, no fee charged by the platform itself, and no deadline of its own: every institution sets its own opening and closing dates.
excerpt: What are the program application deadlines for B.C. colleges and universities? Each institution sets their own application open and close dates. [...] Fees are charged for each application and paid directly to the school. No fees are charged or paid to EducationPlannerBC. [...] Contact information to the 25 public post-secondary institution's listed on the EducationPlannerBC website can be found here.
interpretation: EducationPlannerBC looks like Ontario's OUAC and behaves differently in the way that matters. The OUAC rations choices and charges for them; EducationPlannerBC rations nothing and charges nothing, and the fee and the deadline both belong to the institution. So a student comparing the two provinces should not carry either model across: in British Columbia there is no cost to adding a fourth choice and no central date to aim at, and in Ontario there is both.

excerpt: General admission requirements. IB Diploma Programme: Completed IB Diploma, including at least three Higher Level courses. [...] IB Math Applications and Interpretations SL, or IB Math Studies, do not satisfy the math requirement for admission to UBC's science-based programs, the Faculty of Management, the UBC Sauder School of Business, or the Vancouver School of Economics. [...] Initial admission decisions are based on interim grades as reported by your high school. Once your final IB results are available, we will use them to confirm your admission decision and any first-year credit you may be eligible for. [...] For students who complete the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma, admission to the University will require a minimum of 24 points including bonus points. However, due to limited enrolment, a higher score will be required for admission to most programs. A minimum final grade of "3" in IB English A (Language and Literature) or IB English A (Literature) (Standard or Higher Level) is required for all programs.
interpretation: This is the clearest published answer anywhere in this Destination to the July problem: UBC decides on interim grades and uses the final results only to confirm. So the IB results date of 6 July 2027 is not a decision point, it is a condition, and a student who drops below the offer loses a place they already held rather than one they were waiting for. Note also that UBC counts bonus points where Toronto explicitly does not — two universities in the same country reading the same transcript three points apart, which is exactly why no national conversion is recorded here.

interpretation: The phrasing to read carefully is 'a 5 or better on each subject', which is a floor per subject and not a total.
